newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Britain scales down fish "quota hoppers" battle.
newsitem.headline: Britain scales down fish "quota hoppers" battle.

text.p: Britain will fight to get rid of fishing "quota hoppers" but it does not intend to veto a review of the European Union treaty, British Agriculture Minister Jack Cunningham said on Monday.

Britain's former Conservative government had said that it would block the review by a key inter-governmental conference (IGC) in Amsterdam in June unless the 15-nation bloc changed its fishing policies.
"Quota hopping is a priority for us," Cunningham told a news briefing after a getting-to-know-you meeting with EU Agriculture Commissioner Franz Fischler.
But he added, "I don't expect it to be central to the progress in discussions in the IGC."
The conference is discussing changes in the way the EU operates in preparation for the admission of up to 10 east European countries.
Quota hopping is the practice whereby foreign fishermen have legally set up flag of convenience operations in Britain and bought licences giving them a share of British catch quotas.
The conservatives had argued that it was a crazy situation in which foreign vessels, mainly Spanish and Dutch, now take over one quarter of the British fish catch quota.
Cunningham said he hoped that the new Labour government's more constructive approach to Europe would enable progress to be made in solving the quota-hopper problem.
"We are not going to downgrade the importance of it at all," he insisted. "It will be on our agenda but not in any threatening way."
